title: Next Greater Element I
statement: nums1 is a subset of nums2 (all values distinct). For each x in nums1, find x's position in nums2 and return the first larger value to its right in nums2, or -1 if there is none.

hints.1_question: For every value in nums2 you could find its next greater element once and remember it. What structure lets you do that in one pass?
hints.2_nudge: Scan nums2 with a stack of values still waiting for a bigger one. When a bigger value arrives, it is the answer for everything it pops.
hints.3_big_hint: For x in nums2: while stack and stack[-1] < x: nxt[stack.pop()] = x; push x. Answer = [nxt.get(v, -1) for v in nums1].

known_bugs.name: only looks at the immediate next element in nums2
known_bugs.followup: What if the next greater value is not directly adjacent in nums2?

known_bugs.name: returns 0 instead of -1 when nothing is greater
known_bugs.followup: What does the problem say to return when there is no greater element?

known_bugs.name: rescans nums2 from scratch for each query (O(n * m))
known_bugs.followup: How long does nums2.index(x) plus the scan take per query? What could you precompute for every value at once?

followups: Why does a value get popped at most once?
